AI.tldr: The paper argues for AI-augmented human intelligence (AHI), in which a lifelong personal system called a cognitive symbiont augments what a person can hold and do, alongside artificial general intelligence. It outlines a design space of sensing, keeping, understanding, living alongside, acting, thinking and growing, bounded by a personal runtime and trust.
AI.motivation: Progress in AI is usually measured by what machines can do alone, while people still forget, miss things and lack their own history when the helpful machine stands outside the situation.
AI.method: The authors give the paradigm a conceptual core, the cognitive gap between what a person could bring to a situation and what they can hold in working memory. They organise the design space as a symbiosis loop of sensing, keeping, understanding, living alongside, acting for and thinking with the person, and growing.
AI.result: No empirical results are reported; the contribution is a conceptual framework. The authors identify risks such as covert assistance in examinations and pressure on everyone to adopt the technology, and they treat governance of these risks as part of the paradigm.
AI.conclusion: Physical AI should include a second kind of intelligent individual, the AI-augmented person, and the design and governance of cognitive symbionts should be treated as central to that paradigm.

title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
comment: Project Page: this https URL
summary: Learning a universal action representation from video requires modeling dynamics that are consistent across different executions of the same action yet invariant to changes in embodiment and appearance. Existing latent action models infer actions from visual transitions, but their representations often entangle the underlying action with irrelevant visual variations, limiting transfer across embodiments. We introduce DreamX, which repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a universal latent action learner. Our approach extracts compact latent actions from the video model's rich spatiotemporal features, compressing each latent video frame by $\boldsymbol{300\times}$ ($\boldsymbol{1{,}200 \rightarrow 4}$ tokens). In addition, by leveraging the video model's generative prior, these latent actions capture action-relevant dynamics disentangled from visual appearance. The resulting latent space serves as a shared action interface across embodiments (human and robot), environments, and action parameterizations. On LARY-Bench, DreamX achieves state-of-the-art performance among latent action models. Moreover, actions encoded in one setting remain effective in another: the latent space supports any-to-any video transfer and zero-shot action transfer across diverse embodiments and environments. Furthermore, this shared interface also enables policy learning in a compact latent action space, reducing the computational cost of video-diffusion-based policies.

AI.tldr: DreamX repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a universal latent action learner, compressing each latent video frame 300 times (1,200 to 4 tokens). The resulting action space transfers across human and robot embodiments and environments and achieves state-of-the-art results among latent action models on LARY-Bench.
AI.motivation: Existing latent action models infer actions from visual transitions, but their representations entangle actions with irrelevant visual variation, which limits transfer across embodiments.
AI.method: The method extracts compact latent actions from the spatiotemporal features of a pretrained video diffusion model, relying on the model's generative prior to separate action-relevant dynamics from appearance.
AI.result: On LARY-Bench, DreamX achieves state-of-the-art performance among latent action models. Actions encoded in one setting remain effective in another, supporting any-to-any video transfer and zero-shot action transfer across embodiments and environments. Policy learning in the compact latent space reduces the computational cost of video-diffusion-based policies.
AI.conclusion: The latent space serves as a shared action interface across embodiments, environments and action parameterisations, and it makes video-diffusion policies cheaper to learn.

title: Nonparametric GARCH: An Iterated Neural Estimator
summary: We study nonparametric estimation and forecasting for GARCH-type processes and propose an iterated neural estimator that alternates between estimating the recursion map and updating the unobserved conditional variances. Under mild conditions, we establish finite-sample bounds for the time-averaged in-sample variance-path error and show that the estimator is minimax rate-optimal up to logarithmic factors. Under stationarity and mixing conditions, we establish the same rate for recursion-map estimation and derive finite-sample bounds for out-of-sample variance forecasts and expected excess Gaussian quasi-likelihood (QLIKE) loss. The convergence rates depend on the true lag orders and remain unchanged when the fitted orders are overspecified. Simulation studies illustrate the effectiveness of our estimators under nonlinear and time-varying volatility dynamics. Real-data applications suggest that our neural methods perform competitively and can incorporate option-price and high-frequency information.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes an iterated neural estimator for nonparametric GARCH-type processes that alternates between estimating the recursion map and updating unobserved conditional variances. It is minimax rate-optimal up to logarithmic factors and extends the results to out-of-sample variance forecasts.
AI.motivation: Parametric GARCH models may misspecify nonlinear and time-varying volatility dynamics, and nonparametric estimation of GARCH-type recursions with unobserved variances needs finite-sample guarantees.
AI.method: The estimator alternates between fitting the recursion map with neural networks and updating the unobserved conditional variances, and the analysis covers in-sample variance-path error, recursion-map estimation and forecasting under stationarity and mixing conditions.
AI.result: The authors prove finite-sample bounds for the time-averaged in-sample variance-path error and show minimax rate-optimality up to logarithmic factors. They derive finite-sample bounds for out-of-sample variance forecasts and expected excess Gaussian QLIKE loss. The rates depend on the true lag orders and do not change when the fitted orders are overspecified. Simulations and real-data applications show competitive performance, including use of option-price and high-frequency information.
AI.conclusion: Neural nonparametric estimators can attain optimal rates for GARCH-type volatility models and remain robust to overspecified lag orders.

title: Latent Cluster Separation as a Regularizer for Lifelong Anomaly Detection
comment: 10 pages, 1 figure
summary: Lifelong (continual) anomaly detection systems must learn a sequence of tasks without forgetting how to recognize anomaly types seen earlier -- a property known as backward transfer. A common way to try to improve backward transfer is to reshape a model's internal representation around learnable concept centroids, typically coupled with a new way of scoring anomalies based on distance to those centroids. Because these two design choices are usually introduced together, it is unclear which one is actually responsible for any performance gain. In this paper, we unbundle the two mechanisms within a VAE-based lifelong anomaly detector and study them separately. We find that used purely as a training-time regularizer -- while leaving anomaly scoring unchanged -- latent cluster separation can improve detection quality and backward transfer, though whether it outperforms the alternative scoring approach depends on the dataset's underlying representation. Switching to distance-based scoring is instead where most of the instability commonly associated with this class of method actually originates; we identify and explain the underlying mechanism. This benefit depends on the dataset's underlying representation, and we report this as practical guidance for choosing between the two design choices, rather than as a list of caveats.

AI.tldr: The paper separates two mechanisms in VAE-based lifelong anomaly detection, latent cluster separation and distance-based scoring, and finds that latent cluster separation used only as a training regulariser can improve detection and backward transfer. Distance-based scoring is where most of the instability originates.
AI.motivation: Methods that improve backward transfer usually introduce centroid-based representation learning and centroid-distance scoring together, so it is unclear which component causes any gain.
AI.method: Within a VAE-based lifelong anomaly detector, the two mechanisms are unbundled and studied separately, with anomaly scoring left unchanged when cluster separation is used as a regulariser.
AI.result: Used purely as a training-time regulariser, latent cluster separation can improve detection quality and backward transfer, although whether it beats the alternative scoring approach depends on the dataset's underlying representation. Switching to distance-based scoring is where most instability originates, and the authors explain the mechanism.
AI.conclusion: The authors give practical guidance for choosing between the two design choices, noting that the benefit of cluster separation depends on the dataset's representation.

title: Beyond Proposals: Region-Consistent Open-Set Object Detection
summary: Open-set object detection (OSOD) suffers from a fundamental limitation under dense proposal mechanisms: highly overlapping proposals associated with the same object are often assigned contradictory known/unknown predictions. Existing methods perform open-set reasoning independently for each proposal, while ignoring the shared semantics among correlated proposals, resulting in fragmented detections and unstable open-set decisions. In this paper, we reformulate OSOD as an object-centric semantic inference problem, where correlated proposals jointly support a coherent region-level semantic decision. Based on this perspective, we propose OCSI-Net, a unified framework that combines object-centric semantic consistency with geometry-aware uncertainty stabilization. Specifically, OCSI-Net aggregates correlated proposals into structured region clusters and infers region-level semantics from aggregated semantic evidence, thereby enforcing coherent open-set predictions within the same object region. Furthermore, a geometry-aware uncertainty mechanism is introduced to stabilize optimization near open-set transition boundaries. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that OCSI-Net consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving the harmonic mean of known and unknown detection by an average of 6.83\% over the second-best method.

AI.tldr: OCSI-Net reformulates open-set object detection as object-centric semantic inference, aggregating correlated proposals into region clusters so that each object receives a consistent known or unknown decision. It improves the harmonic mean of known and unknown detection by an average of 6.83 percent over the second-best method.
AI.motivation: Under dense proposals, overlapping proposals for the same object often receive contradictory known or unknown predictions, because existing methods reason about each proposal independently.
AI.method: OCSI-Net groups correlated proposals into structured region clusters and infers region-level semantics from aggregated evidence. A geometry-aware uncertainty mechanism stabilises optimisation near open-set transition boundaries.
AI.result: OCSI-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks, improving the harmonic mean of known and unknown detection by an average of 6.83 percent over the second-best method.
AI.conclusion: Region-level semantic consistency reduces fragmented detections and unstable open-set decisions within the same object region.

title: FlowRig: Unified Skeleton Generation for 3D and 4D Meshes via Flow Matching
comment: Project page: this https URL
summary: Automatic rigging is a fundamental task for both static 3D and dynamic 4D mesh animation, yet existing methods do not provide a unified feedforward solution for these two settings. While static 3D riggers achieve strong quality, they often provide limited control over bone count and become temporally unstable when applied frame by frame to dynamic meshes. Existing 4D methods, in contrast, typically rely on expensive per-sequence optimization. We propose MoTWorld, a template-free, data-efficient framework for unified 3D and 4D skeleton generation. Built on flow matching, MoTWorld generates temporally aligned skeletons for an entire sequence in a single feedforward pass, while naturally handling single-mesh 3D rigging. The model further supports explicit skeleton-count control, uncertainty estimation for candidate selection, and masking-based interpolation, forecasting, and backcasting. To address limited paired 4D rigging data, we adopt a curriculum that initializes from large-scale 3D rigging data and adapts to mid-scale 4D mesh-skeleton data. Experiments show that MoTWorld achieves strong static 3D rigging performance with controllable bone complexity, as well as high-quality and temporally consistent 4D reconstruction and prediction results.

AI.tldr: MoTWorld is a flow-matching framework that generates temporally aligned skeletons for 3D meshes and 4D mesh sequences in a single feedforward pass. It supports controllable bone count and temporal consistency, and it is trained through a curriculum that starts from large 3D rigging data.
AI.motivation: Static 3D riggers offer limited bone-count control and become temporally unstable when applied frame by frame, while 4D methods typically need expensive per-sequence optimisation.
AI.method: The framework is template-free and built on flow matching, with explicit skeleton-count control, uncertainty estimation for candidate selection, and masking-based interpolation, forecasting and backcasting. A curriculum initialises from large-scale 3D rigging data and adapts to mid-scale 4D mesh-skeleton data.
AI.result: The authors report strong static 3D rigging performance with controllable bone complexity, along with high-quality and temporally consistent 4D reconstruction and prediction. No specific numbers are given in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: A single feedforward model can handle both static and dynamic rigging, reducing reliance on per-sequence optimisation and limited paired 4D data.

title: Geometric Refinement and Distributional Alignment for Sim2Real Roadside LiDAR Detection
comment: 8 pages. 1st place, Track 6 (UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR, LUMPI), DriveX Grand Challenge, ECCV 2026 Workshop. Code: this https URL
summary: We describe our approach to the LUMPI track of the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge, in which a 3D object detector must be trained exclusively on synthetic data and evaluated on unseen real roadside LiDAR, while the synthetic point clouds are simultaneously scored for distributional realism. Our final entry scores 0.4793 combined, from a detection mAP of 0.1333 and a realism score of 0.9126. Our contribution is not a new architecture. Working from a PointPillars baseline, we obtained most of our gains from three sources. First, a diagnosis that small object failure in roadside LiDAR is a localisation problem rather than a detection problem, which led to a parameter free geometric refinement worth 86 percent relative on pedestrian AP. Second, an audit of our own post processing which revealed that a shipped rule was destroying valid predictions, the repair of which produced our single largest detection gain at 335 percent relative on the Van class. Third, treating the realism metrics analytically rather than as a black box, which showed that one of the four components is a closed form function of nine summary statistics. We also report an experimental methodology that we believe is the more transferable result. Because mean AP decomposes into independent per class terms, a single submission can carry several mutually controlled experiments, and a submission assembled entirely from previously measured components has a score that is known before it is sent. We predicted our final score to four decimal places prior to submission. We report negative results at equal length, and give a full account of data provenance and compliance in Section 8, including a full account of every mechanism contributing to the submitted score.

AI.tldr: The LUMPI-track entry to the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge trains a PointPillars detector only on synthetic data and reaches 0.4793 combined score, with detection mAP 0.1333 and realism score 0.9126. The gains come from geometric refinement, a post-processing repair and analytical treatment of the realism metrics rather than a new architecture.
AI.motivation: The challenge requires detection on unseen real roadside LiDAR from synthetic training data while the synthetic clouds are also scored for distributional realism.
AI.method: Starting from a PointPillars baseline, the authors apply a parameter-free geometric refinement for localisation of small objects, audit a shipped post-processing rule that was suppressing valid predictions, and analyse the realism metrics, one of whose four components is a closed-form function of nine summary statistics.
AI.result: Geometric refinement gave 86 percent relative gain on pedestrian AP, and repairing the post-processing rule gave a 335 percent relative gain on the Van class, the largest detection gain. The final score was predicted to four decimal places before submission, and negative results are reported at equal length.
AI.conclusion: The more transferable contribution is the methodology: because mean AP decomposes into per-class terms, a submission can carry several controlled experiments, and its score can be predicted from measured components.

title: FlowBench: Counterfactual Imagination Training for Spatial Intelligence
summary: Humans imagine scene changes under hypothetical motions, an ability central to spatial reasoning and robotic planning. However, this capability remains underexplored in vision-language models and world models. We formalize this capability as Counterfactual Spatial Imagination (CSI) and introduce FlowBench, a resource for training and evaluating both, with 428K training examples spanning simulated and real-world scenes, household environments and tabletop manipulation, and diverse question types. A scalable, fully automatic pipeline pairs each hypothetical motion with spatial questions and, in simulation, exact outcome frames and optical flow. For VLMs, proprietary models exhibit an imagination gap, performing worse when motion outcomes must be inferred than when observed, and open-source models perform near chance; fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B on FlowBench-Sim-Train raises its accuracy by 29.5 percentage points in simulation and 16.9 on real images, a strong sim-to-real transfer. For world models, training on FlowBench-Sim improves text-to-flow prediction for all four model families we test, raising the accuracy of Psi-0.6 from 52.1% to 61.7%. FlowBench thus serves as a training and evaluation resource for both. Code and datasets are released at this https URL.

AI.tldr: FlowBench formalises Counterfactual Spatial Imagination and provides 428K training examples for training and evaluating vision-language models and world models on hypothetical motions. Fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B raises its accuracy by 29.5 points in simulation and 16.9 points on real images, and training on FlowBench-Sim improves text-to-flow prediction across four world-model families.
AI.motivation: Imagining scene changes under hypothetical motions is central to spatial reasoning and robotic planning, but it is underexplored in vision-language models and world models.
AI.method: A fully automatic pipeline pairs each hypothetical motion with spatial questions and, in simulation, with exact outcome frames and optical flow. The dataset spans simulated and real scenes, household and tabletop manipulation, and diverse question types.
AI.result: Proprietary VLMs show an imagination gap, performing worse when motion outcomes must be inferred than when they are observed, and open-source models perform near chance. Fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B on FlowBench-Sim-Train gives +29.5 points in simulation and +16.9 on real images. For world models, training on FlowBench-Sim raises Psi-0.6 accuracy from 52.1 to 61.7 percent, across all four families tested.
AI.conclusion: FlowBench serves as a training and evaluation resource for counterfactual spatial imagination and shows sim-to-real transfer.

title: Coordinate Frame Recovery, Per Class NMS and Null Return Modelling for Sim2Real V2X LiDAR Detection
comment: 8 pages. 1st place, Track 7 (UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR, V2X-Real), DriveX Grand Challenge, ECCV 2026 Workshop. Code: this https URL
summary: We describe our approach to the V2X-Real track of the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge, in which a 3D object detector must be trained exclusively on synthetic data and evaluated on unseen real roadside LiDAR from an Ouster OS1-64 unit, while the synthetic point clouds are simultaneously scored for distributional realism. Our final entry scores 0.7457 combined, from a detection mAP of 0.4382 and a realism score of 0.9251. Three findings account for most of our result, and all three were diagnostic rather than architectural. First, a coordinate frame mismatch between our predictions and the evaluation ground truth was suppressing detection AP entirely; recovering it took our score from 0.3520 to 0.5147 in a single submission. Second, a single global non maximum suppression threshold was destroying genuine pedestrian detections, because pedestrians occur in groups and a 0.3 IoU threshold applied to a 0.7 m box suppresses distinct neighbouring people; correcting this per class raised overall mAP from 0.0751 to 0.4295. Third, approximately 31 percent of the real reference point cloud consists of null returns encoded as the literal point (0, 0, 0), a format feature entirely absent from our synthetic clouds, which pinned Earth Mover's Distance near its floor until we modelled it. Negative results are reported at equal length, and Section 9 gives a full account of data provenance and compliance. That section also accounts for every mechanism contributing to the submitted score.

AI.tldr: The V2X-Real entry to the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge reaches a combined score of 0.7457, with detection mAP 0.4382 and realism score 0.9251, using a detector trained only on synthetic data. Three diagnostic fixes account for most of the result rather than architectural changes.
AI.motivation: The detector must generalise from synthetic clouds to real roadside Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR, and the synthetic data must also appear realistic under the challenge metrics.
AI.method: The authors fix a coordinate frame mismatch between predictions and ground truth, replace a single global non-maximum suppression threshold with a per-class threshold, and model the null returns (literal point (0, 0, 0)) found in about 31 percent of the real point clouds, which are absent from the synthetic data.
AI.result: Correcting the coordinate frame raised the score from 0.3520 to 0.5147 in one submission. Per-class NMS raised mAP from 0.0751 to 0.4295, because a 0.3 IoU threshold was suppressing neighbouring pedestrians. Modelling null returns addressed an Earth Mover's Distance term that had been stuck near its floor.
AI.conclusion: Diagnostic corrections to data format and post-processing mattered more than architecture in this challenge, and negative results are reported at equal length.

title: Do We Still Need Rotation-Invariant Architectures? A Statistical Robustness Benchmark for Point Cloud Classification
comment: Accepted to 2nd Round of WACV 2027, 24 pages (8 main + appendix). Website: this https URL
summary: A substantial line of work builds rotation invariance directly into point cloud architectures. We benchmark 10 architectures (PointNet, PointNet++, DGCNN, RIConv, RIConv++, RISurConv, PointMLP, PointTransformer, and the equivariant VN-PointNet and VN-DGCNN) across 5 domains under pose, noise, and occlusion, and analyze the results with confirmatory hypothesis tests rather than point estimates. The three rotation-invariant (RI) architectures achieve the best pose robustness but rank among the lowest on noise robustness in 4 of 5 domains. We ask whether this cost is intrinsic to invariance or specific to how invariance is obtained. We retrain all 10 architectures unchanged, with a simple invariance loss on the embedding and three training seeds each, and evaluate all models on the independently designed ModelNet40-C. Invariance training transfers narrowly but reliably. It improves exactly the corruption families its perturbations target wherever the baseline has headroom (mean occlusion +10.5, lidar +13.4 percentage points of accuracy). At matched training budget the best standard backbone and the best RI architecture end on par on unseen corruptions (within 2.5 percentage points in every seed), and invariance-trained RIConv++ is the most seed-stable top model. Once rotation augmentation is widened, standard backbones concede only a flat, angle-independent accuracy offset under full-sphere rotation. We release the benchmark along with a package for analyzing point cloud robustness and reproducing our results.

AI.tldr: The paper benchmarks ten point-cloud architectures under pose, noise and occlusion across five domains, and finds that rotation-invariant architectures are the most pose-robust but among the least noise-robust. Invariance-style training narrows the gap, and the best standard backbone and best rotation-invariant architecture end on par on unseen corruptions.
AI.motivation: Rotation invariance is built directly into many point-cloud architectures, but its cost in robustness to other corruptions is not established with confirmatory statistics.
AI.method: Ten architectures, including PointNet, DGCNN, RIConv++, VN-DGCNN and PointTransformer, were tested with confirmatory hypothesis tests. The authors then retrained all ten with a simple invariance loss on the embedding and three seeds each, and evaluated on ModelNet40-C.
AI.result: The three rotation-invariant architectures achieve the best pose robustness and rank among the lowest on noise robustness in four of five domains. Invariance training improves the corruption families it targets, with mean occlusion accuracy up 10.5 points and lidar up 13.4 points. At matched budget the best standard and best rotation-invariant backbones are within 2.5 points on unseen corruptions in every seed. Under full-sphere rotation, standard backbones show only a flat, angle-independent accuracy offset.
AI.conclusion: The cost of rotation invariance is largely specific to how invariance is obtained and not intrinsic, and invariance-trained RIConv++ is the most seed-stable top model.

title: SurgEye: Instruction Tuning-Free Perception-Reasoning Framework for Surgical Scene Understanding
summary: Surgical scene understanding is pivotal for computer-assisted intervention, yet demands compositional reasoning across instruments, anatomy, and workflow. Existing surgical vision-language models rely on instruction tuning with large-scale question-answer pairs, entailing laborious data curation and costly retraining. To bridge this gap, we propose SurgEye, a perception-reasoning framework that grounds reasoning in a vision foundation model without instruction tuning. Specifically, we devise Routed Multi-Task Perception (RMP) that routes the vision foundation model through task-specific pathways learned from public perception labels, producing spatial and temporal evidence. We further introduce Agentic Compositional Reasoning (ACR) that employs a frozen large language model to coordinate RMP specialists and temporal memory as callable tools, composing evidence across tasks and time into grounded answers. Moreover, we construct SurgEye-Bench spanning eight surgical procedures, pairing each question with perception labels for verifiable evaluation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SurgEye outperforms state-of-the-arts in surgical reasoning. The source code will be available.

AI.tldr: SurgEye is a perception-reasoning framework for surgical scene understanding that uses a frozen vision foundation model and a frozen LLM without instruction tuning. It routes perception tasks through specialist pathways and composes their evidence with temporal memory, and it is evaluated on a new benchmark, SurgEye-Bench, spanning eight procedures.
AI.motivation: Existing surgical vision-language models rely on instruction tuning with large question-answer datasets, which is costly to curate and retrain.
AI.method: Routed Multi-Task Perception trains task-specific pathways on public perception labels to produce spatial and temporal evidence. Agentic Compositional Reasoning uses a frozen LLM to coordinate these specialists and a temporal memory as callable tools.
AI.result: The abstract reports that SurgEye outperforms state-of-the-art methods in surgical reasoning on SurgEye-Bench, with questions paired with perception labels for verifiable evaluation. No specific numbers are given in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: Grounded reasoning over a vision foundation model can replace instruction tuning for surgical scene understanding, and the source code is stated to be forthcoming.

title: Compression Forcing: Hierarchical History Tokenization Enables Flexible World Models
comment: 37 pages, 16 figures
summary: Effective world modeling requires compressing salient history information that facilitates future prediction. However, most existing approaches inherit tokenization and conditioning mechanisms from video generation, where objectives are centered around perceptual realism rather than predictive utility. This discrepancy limits the world model's effectiveness, especially in environments dominated by visual nuisances or task-irrelevant background details. To this end, we introduce Compression Forcing (CF), a general framework that aligns history compression with the predictive objective of world modeling. Compression Forcing features Dynamics-Aware Tokenization (DAT), a novel tokenization method that compresses history observations into a sequence ordered by decreasing dynamics saliency. Built on a diffusion backbone, this structure enables Hierarchical History Guidance (HG-H), allowing selective amplification of dynamics-salient information during inference. Extensive experiments across various environments demonstrate improved prediction fidelity, physical realism, and downstream decision-making performance, establishing Compression Forcing as a highly flexible and effective approach for world modeling.

AI.tldr: Compression Forcing compresses history for world models into a sequence ordered by dynamics saliency, rather than by perceptual realism, and enables selective amplification of dynamics-salient history at inference. The authors report better prediction fidelity, physical realism and downstream decision-making across environments.
AI.motivation: World models often inherit tokenisation and conditioning from video generation, which is aimed at perceptual realism and not at predictive utility, so visual nuisances can dominate.
AI.method: Dynamics-Aware Tokenisation compresses history observations into a sequence ordered by decreasing dynamics saliency. On a diffusion backbone, Hierarchical History Guidance selectively amplifies dynamics-salient information during inference.
AI.result: The abstract reports improved prediction fidelity, physical realism and downstream decision-making performance across various environments, without specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Aligning history compression with the predictive objective gives a flexible and effective approach to world modelling.

title: Do Pretrained Backbones Transfer to Physical Sensors? A Systematic Study of Multimodal Initialization Across the Sensor Stack
comment: Accepted at WACV 2027. 22 pages (10 main, including references, and 12 supplementary), 4 figures, 13 tables
summary: Transfer learning from pretrained backbones has become standard practice in multi-sensor computer vision---yet two questions remain open: which pretrained weights transfer best to multi-sensor setups, and can in-domain pretraining outperform off-the-shelf solutions? Frameworks like MultiMAE demonstrate the utility of masked autoencoding in a multi-modal context, but rely entirely on dense, model-derived modalities. It is unclear how robustly these methods translate to real-world applications that use physical sensors, where the aggregation of diverse public datasets for large-scale pretraining inherently introduces modality sparsity. To investigate this systematically, we curate a multi-sensor autonomous driving collection of $2.82M$ images from 16 publicly available datasets, incorporating both physical hardware modalities (RGB, LWIR, NIR, Event) and model-derived modalities (Stereo Depth, Segmentation). We use this collection for in-domain pretraining based on the MultiMAE approach. We adapt MultiMAE's loss formulation to accommodate sparse samples, and study the effect of an enforced encoder bottleneck for modality alignment and of additional losses specific to dense reconstruction (SSIM and FFT). We then systematically compare against common pretrained backbones (ViT, MAE, DINO and MultiMAE) across downstream sensor fusion tasks. We find that MultiMAE is a surprisingly strong out-of-the-box baseline, transferring effectively even to modalities it has never seen, while our targeted modifications yield incremental but consistent improvements on multi-sensor transfer and overall robustness.

AI.tldr: The paper systematically tests pretrained backbones for multi-sensor autonomous driving, using 2.82M images from 16 public datasets, and finds that MultiMAE is a surprisingly strong out-of-the-box baseline. Targeted modifications give incremental but consistent gains in transfer and robustness.
AI.motivation: It is unclear which pretrained weights transfer best to physical multi-sensor setups, where pooling public datasets introduces modality sparsity, and whether in-domain pretraining can beat off-the-shelf models.
AI.method: The authors curate a collection covering physical modalities (RGB, LWIR, NIR, Event) and model-derived modalities (Stereo Depth, Segmentation), pretrain with MultiMAE adapted to sparse samples, and study an encoder bottleneck for modality alignment and extra SSIM and FFT losses. They compare against ViT, MAE, DINO and MultiMAE backbones on downstream sensor-fusion tasks.
AI.result: MultiMAE transfers effectively even to modalities it has never seen. The targeted modifications yield incremental but consistent improvements in multi-sensor transfer and overall robustness. No specific numbers are given in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: In-domain MultiMAE pretraining with the proposed modifications is a useful but incremental improvement over strong off-the-shelf baselines for multi-sensor driving.

title: Spatial and Temporal Super-Resolution and Denoising of Intracardiac 4D Flow MRI
summary: Intracardiac flow is driven by complex, and time-varying cardiac motion and interaction with the heart valves, producing complex flow features that may provide valuable information for disease diagnosis and treatment planning. 4D Flow MRI enables non-invasive, time-resolved measurement of three-dimensional cardiovascular velocity fields. However, substantial noise and limited spatial and temporal resolution limit its ability to accurately resolve flow features. We propose 4D-MRAR (4D Magnetic Resonance Augmented Reconstruction), a deep learning (DL) method to super-resolve and denoise 4D Flow MRI data. Unlike prior DL methods that train and infer on static vascular regions, our method predicts intracardiac flow within hearts undergoing large deformation. Moreover, it uniquely allows for simultaneous super-resolution in 3D space and time. The method combines a residual convolutional neural network, a recurrent neural network, and an implicit neural field to predict high-resolution velocity and pressure fields while efficiently enforcing the governing equations of fluid flow during training. Trained on a synthetic dataset obtained from computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of left ventricle (LV) flow, our method generalizes to synthetic whole-heart 4D flow MRI data, and demonstrated promising performance on real 4D Flow MRI. The produced super-resolved flow fields exhibit significantly improved accuracy and greater consistency with the governing equations of blood flow compared with prior methods.

AI.tldr: 4D-MRAR is a deep learning method that jointly super-resolves and denoises 4D Flow MRI of intracardiac flow in beating hearts, combining a residual CNN, a recurrent network and an implicit neural field, with governing fluid equations enforced in training. It generalises from CFD simulations of left-ventricle flow to whole-heart data and shows promising performance on real scans.
AI.motivation: 4D Flow MRI is noisy and has limited spatial and temporal resolution, and prior methods work on static vascular regions rather than hearts undergoing large deformation.
AI.method: The network predicts high-resolution velocity and pressure fields in 3D and time, trained on a synthetic dataset from computational fluid dynamics of left-ventricle flow, with the governing equations enforced during training.
AI.result: The method generalises to synthetic whole-heart 4D Flow MRI and shows promising performance on real 4D Flow MRI. The super-resolved fields show significantly improved accuracy and greater consistency with blood-flow governing equations than prior methods.
AI.conclusion: Physics-constrained neural super-resolution can improve intracardiac 4D Flow MRI, though the abstract's evidence on real data is described as promising rather than conclusive.

title: From Visual Matching to Textual Conditioning: Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation via Reference Inversion
summary: Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation (CD-FSS) aims to segment objects from unseen domains using only a few annotated references. Recent Segment Anything Model (SAM)-based methods have advanced CD-FSS, yet their reference-target visual matching is highly sensitive to target appearance variations. SAM3 introduces text-conditioned segmentation, enabling natural-language descriptions to guide segmentation across target images, but directly using the category name as the condition still yields unstable performance under severe domain shifts. We propose Reference Inversion for SAM3 (RI-SAM3) that leverages SAM3's large-scale vision-language pre-training to learn suitable textual tokens for each target category. RI-SAM3 comprises three core designs: (i) Bi-level Reference Inversion that learns complementary tokens before and after the frozen text encoder: the former remain anchored in SAM3's text space while the latter represent the category more flexibly; (ii) Layer-adaptive Textual Conditioning combines these tokens differently as object queries evolve across decoder layers; and (iii) Presence-aware Confidence Supervision that jointly supervises query confidence and target presence for reliable predictions. With SAM3 frozen, RI-SAM3 optimizes around 12K parameters only per category and it efficiently segments each target in a single forward pass with reusable textual conditioning without per-sample reference-target visual matching. Extensive experiments over multiple widely adopted benchmarks show that RI-SAM3 achieves superior performance consistently in CD-FSS tasks, together with strong robustness, efficiency, and generalization.

AI.tldr: RI-SAM3 adapts a frozen SAM3 to cross-domain few-shot segmentation by learning about 12K parameters per category of textual tokens, instead of matching reference and target visual features. It achieves superior performance across multiple benchmarks with a single forward pass per target.
AI.motivation: SAM-based cross-domain few-shot methods depend on reference-target visual matching, which is sensitive to appearance changes, and using a category name as the text prompt is unstable under severe domain shift.
AI.method: Bi-level Reference Inversion learns tokens before and after the frozen text encoder, Layer-adaptive Textual Conditioning combines them across decoder layers, and Presence-aware Confidence Supervision jointly supervises query confidence and target presence.
AI.result: The abstract reports superior CD-FSS performance across widely used benchmarks, with strong robustness, efficiency and generalisation, but gives no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Learned textual conditioning on a frozen vision-language segmenter can replace per-sample visual matching for cross-domain few-shot segmentation.

title: CHROMA-MILL: Joint Low-Light Enhancement and White Balance under Colored Illumination
comment: Accepted at WACV 2027. 16 pages (main paper + supplementary material), 7 figures, 7 tables. Project page: this https URL
summary: Capturing an image in a low-light environment produces a weak, noisy sensor signal. Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) aims to restore it. Auto white balance (AWB) is also required for every image, and the same noisy signal degrades its ability to infer the scene illuminant. LLIE is typically performed first, followed by AWB, but this strategy remains largely unexamined because existing low-light datasets span a narrow range of illuminants and lack illuminant ground truth for evaluating AWB. We address this with CHROMA-MILL, a RAW dataset of 50 scenes captured with a DSLR and smartphone under four calibrated illuminants at eleven intensity levels. Because light is additive, we blend these captures in the linear RAW domain to synthesize physically valid illuminant mixtures with exact chromaticity ground truth. Benchmarking on this data, we find joint correction is best, and introduce CTI-Retinexformer, which supervises an illumination map, a chromaticity prediction, and an illumination-invariant scene embedding, outperforming the best cascade by 0.7 dB PSNR$_L$ and 1.1 $\Delta E_{00}$.

AI.tldr: CHROMA-MILL is a RAW dataset of 50 scenes under four calibrated illuminants at eleven intensity levels, with synthetic mixtures of illuminants that have exact chromaticity ground truth. The paper introduces CTI-Retinexformer, which jointly corrects low-light enhancement and white balance and outperforms the best cascade by 0.7 dB PSNR-L and 1.1 Delta E00.
AI.motivation: Low-light enhancement is usually followed by auto white balance, but this order is unexamined, and existing low-light datasets cover a narrow range of illuminants and lack illuminant ground truth.
AI.method: Captures were made with a DSLR and a smartphone and blended in the linear RAW domain, which is physically valid because light is additive. CTI-Retinexformer supervises an illumination map, a chromaticity prediction and an illumination-invariant scene embedding.
AI.result: Joint correction is best in the benchmarks, and CTI-Retinexformer outperforms the best cascade by 0.7 dB PSNR-L and 1.1 Delta E00.
AI.conclusion: Joint low-light enhancement and white balance is preferable to a cascade under coloured illumination, and the dataset supports evaluating white balance with ground truth.

title: Is This 3D Asset Usable? Beyond the Beauty Render for Asset Curation
summary: Large 3D repositories make it easy to collect assets, but difficult to determine whether they can be reused reliably across scene assembly, editing, rendering, game production, and training-data construction. An asset can look plausible in RGB while hiding disconnected geometry, problematic UV organization, or materials that fail to resolve correctly after import. We introduce Diagnostic Rendered Evidence (DRE): aligned beauty, wireframe, and UV-seam-plus-wireframe views scored by pass-specific frozen ViT classifiers and combined through late fusion. On 1,234 human labeled TexVerse assets, nested grouped evaluation achieves 86.36% balanced accuracy and 88.32% bad-asset recall. On a separate, balanced 764 external reference test, DRE achieved 88.9% balanced reference-label accuracy. Our method requires only an imported asset and renderer-derived evidence, without repository identity, creator, popularity, text, or source metadata at inference. Our results support cross-corpus portability and show that purpose built diagnostic views expose defects that just the beauty views can miss. Webpage: this https URL

AI.tldr: Diagnostic Rendered Evidence scores a 3D asset's usability with beauty, wireframe and UV-seam-plus-wireframe renders, passed through pass-specific frozen ViT classifiers and late fusion. It reaches 86.36 percent balanced accuracy on 1,234 labelled TexVerse assets and 88.9 percent balanced reference-label accuracy on an external test set of 764 assets.
AI.motivation: Assets that look plausible in RGB can hide disconnected geometry, problematic UV layouts or materials that fail after import, which makes reuse across scenes, games and training data unreliable.
AI.method: The method takes aligned beauty, wireframe and UV-seam views and uses separate frozen ViT classifiers for each pass, combined by late fusion. At inference it needs only the imported asset and renderer-derived evidence, with no repository, creator, text or popularity metadata.
AI.result: On TexVerse, nested grouped evaluation gives 86.36 percent balanced accuracy and 88.32 percent bad-asset recall. On a separate balanced external reference test of 764 assets, balanced reference-label accuracy is 88.9 percent. Purpose-built diagnostic views expose defects that beauty views alone can miss.
AI.conclusion: The approach is portable across corpora, and diagnostic renders are needed in addition to beauty renders for asset curation.

title: Co-Occurrence Priors Override Visual Spatial Evidence: Understanding False Alarms in Vision-Language Models for Construction Struck-By Hazard Detection
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) increasingly support construction hazard monitoring, yet their frequent false alarms remain poorly understood. This study investigates whether false struck-by hazard warnings arise from failures in object recognition, spatial relation encoding, or hazard decisions dominated by learned co-occurrence priors. We evaluated Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3.5-8B using 355 counterfactual worker-excavator scene pairs with controlled spatial proximity and worker-removal variants, combining behavioral analysis, internal representation probing, causal interventions, and decision correction. Both models recognized the entities and encoded their spatial relations (out-of-fold AUROC: 0.82 and 0.91), assigning higher hazard scores to near than far scenes in 79% and 73% of pairs. Nevertheless, 74% and 100% of far scenes were falsely classified as hazardous. Removing the worker reduced Qwen's hazard rate to 11%, while worker presence exerted 2.4- and 3.2-times greater influence on hazard scores than spatial proximity in the respective models. Attention-head interventions, neuron-level interventions, and activation steering failed to eliminate this co-occurrence bias. However, conditioning hazard decisions on the model's own spatial-relation representation improved Qwen's specificity from 0.36 to 0.58 at matched sensitivity, outperforming threshold recalibration. These findings reveal that VLM struck-by false alarms stem primarily from decision-making failures rather than deficiencies in object recognition or spatial encoding, suggesting that future efforts should prioritize conditioning hazard decisions on encoded spatial evidence rather than further improving visual recognition alone.

AI.tldr: Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3.5-8B raise struck-by hazard false alarms on counterfactual worker-excavator scenes mainly because of co-occurrence priors in their decisions, not because they fail to recognise objects or spatial relations. Conditioning the hazard decision on the model's own spatial representation raised Qwen's specificity from 0.36 to 0.58 at matched sensitivity.
AI.motivation: Vision-language models are increasingly used for construction hazard monitoring, but their frequent false alarms are poorly understood, and it is unclear whether they come from recognition, spatial encoding or decision-making.
AI.method: The study used 355 counterfactual worker-excavator scene pairs with controlled proximity and worker-removal variants, combining behavioural analysis, probing of internal representations, causal interventions and decision correction.
AI.result: Both models recognised the entities and encoded spatial relations, with out-of-fold AUROC of 0.82 and 0.91. They gave higher hazard scores to near than far scenes in 79 and 73 percent of pairs, yet 74 and 100 percent of far scenes were falsely flagged. Removing the worker reduced Qwen's hazard rate to 11 percent, and worker presence had 2.4 and 3.2 times more influence on hazard scores than proximity. Attention-head, neuron-level and activation-steering interventions did not remove the bias.
AI.conclusion: False alarms stem mainly from decision-making failures, and future work should condition hazard decisions on encoded spatial evidence rather than only improve visual recognition.

title: ReconDreamer#: Self-Evolving Closed-Loop Synergy of Reconstruction and Generation for Dynamic Driving Scenes
summary: Dynamic driving scene reconstruction has made remarkable strides in recent years by leveraging generative priors, particularly in the quality of novel trajectory rendering. Nevertheless, a significant gap remains between the generated data and real-world sensor observations, severely hindering further improvements in reconstruction fidelity. In this paper, we present ReconDreamer#, a self-evolving framework that synergizes reconstruction and generation for dynamic driving scenes, which substantially bridges the gap between synthesized novel trajectory data and recorded real-world observations. Within this self-evolving closed-loop framework, the generative and reconstruction models mutually reinforce each other through iterative refinement, ultimately yielding a significant enhancement in the 3D representation capability of the reconstruction model. Additionally, we introduce a geometry-prior-based adaptive ground model to further enhance the rendering quality of the reconstruction model. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, we conduct comprehensive evaluations on Waymo, nuScenes, PandaSet, and EUVS benchmarks. Specifically on Waymo, at a 6-m lateral shift, ReconDreamer# improves NTA-IoU and NTL-IoU by 8.8% and 3.0%, respectively, and reduces FID by 15.1% relative to ReconDreamer++.

AI.tldr: ReconDreamer# is a self-evolving closed loop in which a reconstruction model and a generative model improve each other for dynamic driving scenes, narrowing the gap between generated novel-trajectory data and real sensor observations. On Waymo at a 6 m lateral shift it improves NTA-IoU by 8.8 percent and NTL-IoU by 3.0 percent, and reduces FID by 15.1 percent relative to ReconDreamer++.
AI.motivation: Generated novel-trajectory data differs from real sensor observations, which limits reconstruction fidelity in dynamic driving scenes.
AI.method: Reconstruction and generation models are refined iteratively, each reinforcing the other, and a geometry-prior-based adaptive ground model is added to improve rendering quality.
AI.result: Evaluated on Waymo, nuScenes, PandaSet and EUVS, the method improves NTA-IoU by 8.8 percent, NTL-IoU by 3.0 percent and reduces FID by 15.1 percent relative to ReconDreamer++ on Waymo at a 6 m lateral shift.
AI.conclusion: Closed-loop co-evolution of generation and reconstruction improves the 3D representation of the reconstruction model for driving scenes.

title: Statistical Machine Learning for Medicinal Plant Leaves Classification
summary: Medicinal plants are usually identified using practitioners' experience, but reproducible, image based methods can complement this knowledge. We present MEDIPI (MEDIcinal Plant Identification), a statistical machine learning approach that classifies medicinal plant leaves from photographs. From each leaf image we extract 52 interpretable features covering shape, texture, color, and a new scagnostics category. We then classify leaves using a three level hierarchy: shape, then edge type, then species. We also release MedLEA, an open R package with 1,099 leaf images of 31 Sri Lankan medicinal plant species. On this dataset, a hierarchical Random Forest achieved the best overall accuracy (100%) in our comparison of hierarchical and non-hierarchical approaches and eight algorithms: Random Forest, XGBoost, Gradient Boosting, linear discriminant analysis, k-nearest neighbor, support vector machine, probabilistic neural network, and artificial neural network. Adding texture, color, and scagnostic features to shape features raised shape level accuracy from 90% to 97%. Linear discriminant analysis plots show how the trained model separates leaf shapes. Accuracy dropped sharply (23-50%) when training and test data came from different datasets, so generalization across datasets remains a challenge.

AI.tldr: MEDIPI classifies medicinal plant leaves from photographs with 52 interpretable features and a three-level hierarchy of shape, edge type and species. A hierarchical Random Forest reaches 100 percent accuracy on the 1,099-image MedLEA dataset of 31 Sri Lankan species, but accuracy falls to 23 to 50 percent across datasets.
AI.motivation: Medicinal plants are usually identified by practitioners' experience, and reproducible image-based methods could complement this knowledge.
AI.method: Features cover shape, texture, colour and a new scagnostics category. The hierarchy classifies shape first, then edge type, then species, and is compared with non-hierarchical approaches and eight algorithms, including Random Forest, XGBoost, SVM and an artificial neural network. The authors also release MedLEA as an open R package.
AI.result: The hierarchical Random Forest achieved the best overall accuracy of 100 percent on MedLEA. Adding texture, colour and scagnostic features to shape raised shape-level accuracy from 90 to 97 percent. Accuracy dropped to 23 to 50 percent when training and test data came from different datasets.
AI.conclusion: The hierarchical, interpretable approach works well within one dataset, but generalisation across datasets remains a challenge.

title: SettleSplat: Monocular Gaussian Mapping under In-View Scene Changes
comment: Accepted at WACV 2027
summary: Online 3D Gaussian mapping enables fast and high-fidelity novel view synthesis, with broad applications in augmented reality, robotics, and autonomous systems. However, many current methods assume static scenes or filter out dynamics as outliers. In this paper, we study in-view scene changes where objects are manipulated in front of the camera within a single online sequence, unlike prior works that detect changes outside the camera view or between separate captures. This setting entangles transient and persistent dynamics, as objects can be distractors while moving and persistent once they settle. While recent studies start to address distractors by removing them for clean static background, in-view scene changes remain underexplored. To resolve this, we present SettleSplat, a monocular mapping system that maintains up-to-date 3D Gaussian maps under such changes. Specifically, we lift coarse per-pixel uncertainty into Gaussian dynamicity field, then prune transient ones. For persistent changes, we derive geometric contradictions weighted by parameter-free rendered depth uncertainty to separate true changes from under-optimized regions. On Bonn and Co-Fusion, SettleSplat achieves consistent 3D Gaussian maps, outperforming current baselines on both full images and change regions while maintaining comparable speed.

AI.tldr: SettleSplat is a monocular 3D Gaussian mapping system that keeps maps up to date when objects are moved in front of the camera within one online sequence. It separates transient distractors from persistent changes and outperforms baselines on Bonn and Co-Fusion, both on full images and change regions, at comparable speed.
AI.motivation: Many online Gaussian mapping methods assume static scenes or discard dynamics as outliers, and in-view scene changes, where objects are manipulated in front of the camera, remain underexplored.
AI.method: Coarse per-pixel uncertainty is lifted into a Gaussian dynamicity field, and transient Gaussians are pruned. For persistent changes, geometric contradictions weighted by parameter-free rendered-depth uncertainty separate true changes from under-optimised regions.
AI.result: On Bonn and Co-Fusion, SettleSplat achieves consistent 3D Gaussian maps and outperforms current baselines on both full images and change regions, while maintaining comparable speed. No specific numbers are given in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: Explicit handling of transient and persistent dynamics enables consistent monocular Gaussian maps under in-view changes.

title: LiSA: Linear Stochastic Attention for Long-Range Visual Modeling
summary: Self-attention has become the standard for modern sequence modeling, enabling Transformers to model long-range dependencies across a wide range of modalities. Despite these advances, its quadratic cost with respect to sequence length remains a significant computational bottleneck. Recent work addresses this limitation by introducing linear variants of self-attention, namely with kernel approximations of the softmax operator. However, their first-order aggregation restricts expressivity and struggles to capture higher-order structure. We propose Linear Stochastic Attention (LiSA), a linear attention plug-in module that enables higher-order token interactions via a stochastic diffusion process based on truncated random walks. LiSA incorporates adaptive locality, favoring semantically similar neighbors to preserve fine-grained structures, while maintaining stable and efficient training. We conduct extensive experiments on classification, semantic segmentation, and object detection tasks and show improved results over state-of-the-art methods.

AI.tldr: LiSA is a linear attention module that captures higher-order token interactions through a stochastic diffusion process based on truncated random walks, with adaptive locality that favours semantically similar neighbours. The paper reports improved results over state-of-the-art methods on classification, semantic segmentation and object detection.
AI.motivation: Self-attention is quadratic in sequence length, and existing linear variants rely on kernel approximations of softmax whose first-order aggregation limits expressivity and misses higher-order structure.
AI.method: LiSA is a plug-in linear attention module that uses truncated random walks in a stochastic diffusion process to model higher-order interactions, with adaptive locality to preserve fine-grained structure and stable training.
AI.result: The abstract reports improved results over state-of-the-art methods on classification, semantic segmentation and object detection, without specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Random-walk-based higher-order aggregation can give a linear-cost attention plug-in that improves visual modelling over existing linear attention.

title: Reliability-Role Collaborative Learning for Semi-Supervised Cardiac Image Segmentation
comment: Accepted at IEEE BIBM 2026. 7 pages, 4 figures
summary: Semi-supervised cardiac image segmentation aims to exploit abundant unlabeled images together with limited annotations, but the reliability of pseudo-label supervision is highly uneven across spatial regions. In a dual-network setting, interior regions are usually more stable, whereas boundary regions, low-confidence areas, and disagreements between networks can introduce noisy supervision. However, existing methods typically impose uniform supervision on all unlabeled pixels, overlooking reliability differences and limiting discriminative learning in challenging areas. To address this issue, we propose R2CL (Reliability-Role Collaborative Learning), a framework for semi-supervised cardiac image segmentation. R2CL models confidence relationships between two networks to assign roles to unlabeled regions: mutually uncertain regions are used for entropy regularization, confidence-discrepant regions for directional knowledge transfer, and mutually confident regions as reliable supervision anchors. Reliability-Role Mixed Cross Learning (RR-MCL) implements these roles through region-mixed training, directional cross-network supervision, and entropy regularization over mutually uncertain regions. Reliability-Transition Prototype Contrastive Learning (RT-PCL) constructs query features from foreground-adjacent reliability-transition regions and learns network-specific class prototypes from mutually confident regions, improving feature discrimination around ambiguous boundaries. High-confidence Context Refinement (HCR) exploits reliable interior pixels and trusted dense blocks within mutually confident regions to complement stable contextual supervision. R2CL achieves stable improvements in region-overlap and boundary-related metrics across multiple datasets, with more evident advantages on the foreground-sparse MVAA-CT dataset.

AI.tldr: R2CL assigns roles to unlabelled regions in semi-supervised cardiac segmentation according to the reliability of two networks' predictions, using entropy regularisation, directional transfer and reliable anchors. It shows stable gains in overlap and boundary metrics across datasets, with clearer advantages on the foreground-sparse MVAA-CT dataset.
AI.motivation: Pseudo-label reliability varies across space, with boundaries, low-confidence areas and inter-network disagreements being noisy, yet existing methods apply uniform supervision to all unlabelled pixels.
AI.method: R2CL models confidence relations between two networks. Mutually uncertain regions get entropy regularisation, confidence-discrepant regions get directional knowledge transfer, and mutually confident regions serve as anchors. RR-MCL implements these roles, RT-PCL builds prototype contrastive learning around reliability-transition boundaries, and HCR refines context from reliable interior pixels.
AI.result: The abstract reports stable improvements in region-overlap and boundary metrics across multiple datasets, with more evident advantages on MVAA-CT. No specific numbers are given.
AI.conclusion: Role-based treatment of unlabelled regions by reliability improves semi-supervised cardiac segmentation, especially around ambiguous boundaries.

title: Mamba3R: Fixed-Capacity Selective State Memory for Long-Sequence 3D Reconstruction
comment: 12 pages, 4 figures, 8 tables. The supplementary material referenced in the text is not included in this version
summary: Streaming 3D reconstruction must maintain geometric quality over long inputs within a fixed GPU budget. A pretrained recurrent model provides bounded state, but freezing its backbone also fixes its learned state-observation interactions. We introduce Mamba3R, a jointly designed state-memory adapter that provides a trainable adaptation path without updating the backbone or task heads. A selective state-space mixer jointly transforms native state features and a fixed-capacity auxiliary memory, explicit read and write paths carry information across frames, and a decomposed feedback path regulates what the added memory feeds back. Only 1.28 million adapter parameters are trained. Under a shared periodic-reset protocol, it lowers trajectory error and improves accumulated surface and depth accuracy over recurrent baselines on public indoor and outdoor datasets and robot-recorded traversals, gaining up to 40 percent on one metric. Matched comparisons support both the choice of the mixing operator and the utility of carrying the auxiliary memory across frames. Allocated memory remains unchanged and throughput moves by at most 1.4 percent from one to two thousand frames. Replaying its recorded traversals offline, the platform's RTX 4060 averages 11.7 frames per second within 5.1 GiB with the same checkpoint, a mean throughput covering the 10 Hz sensor rate.

AI.tldr: Mamba3R is a state-memory adapter for streaming 3D reconstruction that trains only 1.28 million parameters on top of a frozen recurrent backbone, using a selective state-space mixer and a fixed-capacity auxiliary memory. It lowers trajectory error and improves surface and depth accuracy over recurrent baselines, with memory and throughput that stay almost constant over long sequences.
AI.motivation: Streaming reconstruction must stay accurate over long inputs within a fixed GPU budget, and freezing a pretrained recurrent backbone fixes its state-observation interactions.
AI.method: Explicit read and write paths carry information across frames, a selective state-space mixer jointly transforms native state features and the auxiliary memory, and a decomposed feedback path regulates what the memory feeds back. Only the adapter is trained.
AI.result: Under a shared periodic-reset protocol, Mamba3R lowers trajectory error and improves surface and depth accuracy on indoor and outdoor datasets and robot traversals, gaining up to 40 percent on one metric. Allocated memory is unchanged and throughput varies by at most 1.4 percent from one to two thousand frames. On an RTX 4060 it averages 11.7 frames per second within 5.1 GiB.
AI.conclusion: A lightweight adapter with a fixed-capacity memory can improve long-sequence reconstruction while keeping cost constant, and its throughput covers a 10 Hz sensor rate.

title: LINDA: Low Resource Foot Ulcer Segmentation using Local Similarity and Iterative Neural Dynamics
summary: Foot ulcers are a leading cause of lower limb amputation, and the highest burden often falls on low and middle income regions where specialists and computing hardware are both scarce. Wound monitoring tools are most useful there when they are accurate yet small enough to run on ordinary devices, but accuracy usually comes from heavy networks. We present LINDA, a compact model that grounds segmentation in an explicit structural prior instead of raw intensity. A Local Self-Similarity (LSS) map, computed directly from the image and stable under local lighting changes, is fused into a ResNet-34 encoder, and a small Liquid Time-Constant module refines the boundary over four iterative steps. With every model trained under one protocol on the FUSeg 2021 dataset, LINDA obtains the best Dice (86.68\%), IoU (79.67\%), and boundary accuracy (HD95 6.37 pixels) in our comparison while using only 25.70M parameters, fewer than the U-Net and transformer baselines. As the LSS map is a fixed function of the input, it exposes the structural cues the model follows in a readable form. Together this makes LINDA an accurate, inspectable, and lightweight option for wound assessment in resource-constrained care.

AI.tldr: LINDA is a compact foot-ulcer segmentation model that fuses a Local Self-Similarity map into a ResNet-34 encoder and refines boundaries with a small Liquid Time-Constant module over four iterative steps. It achieves the best Dice (86.68 percent), IoU (79.67 percent) and HD95 (6.37 pixels) on FUSeg 2021 with 25.70M parameters.
AI.motivation: Wound monitoring is most useful in low- and middle-income regions, where devices are limited, but accurate segmentation usually needs heavy networks.
AI.method: The Local Self-Similarity map is computed directly from the image and is stable under local lighting changes. A small Liquid Time-Constant module refines the boundary iteratively, and all models were trained under one protocol.
AI.result: In the authors' comparison LINDA obtains the best Dice (86.68 percent), IoU (79.67 percent) and HD95 (6.37 pixels) on FUSeg 2021, using 25.70M parameters, fewer than the U-Net and transformer baselines.
AI.conclusion: An explicit structural prior gives an accurate, inspectable and lightweight option for wound assessment in resource-constrained care.

title: TCINet: Tissue-Conditioned Adaptive Cross-Branch Interaction Network for Nuclei Instance Segmentation
comment: Accepted by IEEE BIBM 2026 as a short paper
summary: Separating touching nuclei requires local boundary detail, while cell type classification requires broader morphological context. These requirements also vary with the surrounding tissue environment. We propose the Tissue-Conditioned Adaptive Cross-Branch Interaction Network (TCINet), a single-stage model with Task-Specific Feature Adapters (TSFA) and Tissue-Conditioned Task-Aware Cross-Branch Interaction (TC-TACBI). TSFA produces branch-specific features at skip connections, and TC-TACBI controls three asymmetric paths among nucleus-presence (NP), horizontal-vertical (HV), and nucleus-type (NT) branches using predicted tissue probabilities. On PanNuke under standard three-fold cross-validation, TCINet achieves multiclass and binary panoptic quality scores of 0.519 and 0.692, respectively. Zero-shot tests on MoNuSeg yield a detection F1 score of 0.876. On PanNuke fold 0, adding TC-TACBI increases mPQ from 0.505 to 0.525. Code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: TCINet is a single-stage nuclei instance segmentation network whose branches are conditioned on predicted tissue probabilities through task-specific feature adapters and tissue-conditioned cross-branch interaction. On PanNuke it reaches multiclass and binary panoptic quality of 0.519 and 0.692, and zero-shot detection F1 of 0.876 on MoNuSeg.
AI.motivation: Separating touching nuclei needs fine boundary detail, while cell-type classification needs broader morphological context, and these requirements vary with tissue environment.
AI.method: Task-Specific Feature Adapters produce branch-specific features at skip connections. Tissue-Conditioned Task-Aware Cross-Branch Interaction controls three asymmetric paths among the nucleus-presence, horizontal-vertical and nucleus-type branches using predicted tissue probabilities.
AI.result: Under standard three-fold cross-validation on PanNuke, multiclass and binary panoptic quality are 0.519 and 0.692. Zero-shot on MoNuSeg gives detection F1 of 0.876. On PanNuke fold 0, adding TC-TACBI raises mPQ from 0.505 to 0.525.
AI.conclusion: Conditioning cross-branch interaction on tissue context improves nuclei instance segmentation, with the module adding about 0.02 mPQ on fold 0.

title: Improving Diffusion-Based Augmentation for Data-Scarce Image Classification via Mask-Guided Reference Attention and Repulsive Noise Optimization
comment: WACV2027 accepted
summary: Diffusion-based data augmentation has emerged as a powerful strategy for addressing data-scarce image classification. Recent pipelines typically adapt a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model to a limited number of class examples and subsequently sample synthetic images using diverse textual prompts. However, in extreme data-scarce regimes such as long-tailed single-sample settings, this approach suffers from a dual failure mode: the generated samples often lack discriminative foreground details crucial for classifier training, and the adapted class prior can bias the early denoising process, causing output images to exhibit similar patterns despite varying text prompts. To overcome these limitations, we propose a sampling-side framework of two complementary components that simultaneously enhance fine details and diversity. First, Mask-Guided Reference (MGR) Attention updates only foreground value tokens with reference features via zero-shot segmentation, limiting reference influence to the target object and mitigating excessive global feature injection. Second, Repulsive Noise Optimization (RNO) encourages initial noise trajectories to diverge from dominant generative modes of the adapted model, enabling target prompts to express broader contextual variation. Extensive evaluations show consistent improvements, with the largest gains in long-tailed single-sample settings of up to 2.50 and 2.94 points on CUB-LT IF100, and further robustness across few-shot and background-shift evaluations.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a sampling-side framework for diffusion-based data augmentation in extremely data-scarce classification, combining Mask-Guided Reference attention and Repulsive Noise Optimisation to improve fine foreground detail and sample diversity. Gains reach up to 2.50 and 2.94 points on CUB-LT IF100 in long-tailed single-sample settings.
AI.motivation: Adapted diffusion models in single-sample regimes produce samples that lack discriminative foreground detail, and the adapted class prior makes outputs look similar across varied prompts.
AI.method: Mask-Guided Reference attention updates only foreground value tokens with reference features, using zero-shot segmentation to limit reference influence to the target object. Repulsive Noise Optimisation pushes initial noise trajectories away from the dominant generative modes of the adapted model.
AI.result: The abstract reports consistent improvements, with gains of up to 2.50 and 2.94 points on CUB-LT IF100 in long-tailed single-sample settings, and further robustness in few-shot and background-shift evaluations.
AI.conclusion: Mask-guided reference attention and repulsive noise together improve the fine detail and diversity of diffusion-based augmentation in extreme data scarcity.

title: CounterSketch: Physics-Grounded Counterfactual Reasoning for Sketch-to-Video Generation
summary: Counterfactual sketch animation explores how a static sketch evolves under a hypothetical intervention. We present CounterSketch, a physics-grounded framework that transforms natural-language ``What if...?'' queries into physically plausible sketch animations. The framework integrates VLM-guided scene grounding, causal event-chain reasoning, constraint-based trajectory generation, and verification. It models physical transitions to update the scene graph, computes continuous object trajectories, and validates them against physical, geometric, and semantic constraints. The verified trajectories are then projected into object-level motion bounding boxes to guide downstream sketch-video synthesis. Experiments on CounterSketchBench (80 questions) demonstrate that physics-grounded trajectories provide stronger motion guidance than direct VLM predictions.

AI.tldr: CounterSketch turns natural-language what-if queries into physically grounded sketch animations by combining VLM scene grounding, causal event-chain reasoning, constraint-based trajectories and verification. On CounterSketchBench of 80 questions, physics-grounded trajectories give stronger motion guidance than direct VLM predictions.
AI.motivation: Counterfactual sketch animation asks how a static sketch evolves under a hypothetical intervention, and direct VLM predictions of motion may not be physically plausible.
AI.method: The framework updates a scene graph through modelled physical transitions, computes continuous object trajectories, and validates them against physical, geometric and semantic constraints. Verified trajectories are projected into object-level motion bounding boxes that guide sketch-video synthesis.
AI.result: On CounterSketchBench (80 questions), physics-grounded trajectories provide stronger motion guidance than direct VLM predictions. No specific numbers are given in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: Verified physical trajectories can guide sketch-to-video generation better than direct VLM predictions for counterfactual queries.

title: P-SER: Physical Consistency-Constrained Scattering Expandable Representation for Class-Incremental HRRP Target Recognition
summary: High-resolution range profiles (HRRPs) provide compact radar target representations but exhibit strong aspect sensitivity, complicating class-incremental recognition when historical data are unavailable. Changes in viewing aspect shift scattering-peak locations and amplitudes, while reflector groups may produce responses resembling ships. Existing dynamic expansion methods can also incur substantial parameter and memory overhead. To address these challenges, we propose P-SER, a Physical Consistency-Constrained Scattering Expandable Representation framework for exemplar-free class-incremental HRRP recognition. P-SER reconstructs dominant scattering points from complex-valued sum- and azimuth-difference-channel HRRPs and observation geometry. The reconstructed spatial structure, target extent, and energy distribution are used to derive class-level scattering prototypes and sample-level saliency priors, providing physically grounded constraints for feature learning and old-class knowledge retention. A primitive scatterer dictionary further characterizes local strong-scattering mechanisms and calibrates uncertain ship--reflector predictions at inference. Meanwhile, lightweight residual adapters are incrementally introduced into a shared HRRP backbone to learn new classes with limited model growth. Experiments on simulated and measured HRRP datasets show that P-SER delivers competitive recognition performance without retaining old-class exemplars, while maintaining physical consistency, interference robustness, knowledge retention, and model scalability.

AI.tldr: P-SER is an exemplar-free class-incremental recogniser for high-resolution range profiles that reconstructs dominant scattering points, derives physically grounded prototypes and priors, and adds lightweight residual adapters. It gives competitive recognition on simulated and measured HRRP data while retaining old-class knowledge and limiting model growth.
AI.motivation: HRRP targets are aspect-sensitive, so changes in viewing angle shift scattering peaks, reflector groups can resemble ships, and existing dynamic expansion methods add substantial parameter and memory overhead.
AI.method: Complex-valued sum and azimuth-difference channel profiles and the observation geometry are used to reconstruct dominant scattering points. These yield class-level scattering prototypes and sample-level saliency priors that constrain feature learning, and a primitive scatterer dictionary calibrates uncertain ship-reflector predictions. Lightweight residual adapters are added incrementally to a shared backbone.
AI.result: The abstract reports competitive recognition on simulated and measured HRRP datasets without retaining old-class exemplars, along with physical consistency, interference robustness, knowledge retention and model scalability. No specific numbers are given.
AI.conclusion: Physics-based constraints and scattering-point reconstruction can support class-incremental HRRP recognition without stored exemplars and with limited model growth.

title: ProGeo-RC: Prototype-guided Semantic Reliability and Geometric Error Calibration for Semi-supervised Cardiac Image Segmentation
comment: Accepted at IEEE BIBM 2026. 7 pages, 3 figures
summary: Semi-supervised medical image segmentation aims to train reliable segmentation models using limited labeled data and abundant unlabeled data.
